newsitem.title: USA: MCI results aided by efficiences, long distance.
newsitem.headline: MCI results aided by efficiences, long distance.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp., posted higher fourth quarter profits Tuesday and said volume in its long distance business grew 8 percent in the quarter.
The second largest long distance company reported fourth quarter earnings of $303 million, or 44 cents a share, up from $284 million, or 41 cents a share, a year ago.
Chief Executive Gerald Taylor said MCI had managed to target high value customers without losing existing clients in the mass long distance market.

"The year's results reflect the combination of solid growth in our new high-margin businesses and the strength of our core business," Taylor said. "We are well positioned to take advantage of the key opportunities in front of us."
Revenue for the core long-distance business in the fourth quarter rose 10 percent to $4.3 billion. Local service revenue in the fourth quarter was $49 million, up 23 percent from a year ago.
Wireless revenues in the fourth quarter were $80 million, "down slightly" from the third quarter, and customers served increased to 400,000. No comparison figures were given.

MCI, which is in the process of merging with British Telecommunications Plc, said its Concert joint venture with the British company had fourth quarter revenues of $165 million, up more than $65 million from a year ago.
For the year, MCI earned $1.20 billion, or $1.73 a share, compared with $548 million, or 80 cents a share in 1995. Revenues rose to $18.49 billion from $15.26 billion a year earlier.
MCI stock was up 25 cents at $34.625 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq.
